Brunning kept in front until Cambridge Road, when Charlie Speechley and Eddie Heather went into the lead. At the top of the hill Harry Churcher went in front and went on to win by over half a minute.
The third place went to our "B" team, which, as far as the scoring went, consisted of "Juniors" Eddie Heather, Syd Roberts, Charlie Speechley and Harry Thaxter.

After a small lap of the Common, Clayton was still leading, Eddie Heather having worked his way into second place. These two were still leading at the top of the hills, with Roberts leading Thaxter and Doubleday for third place.
Len Coleman, fourth "A" team man, also moved up, and Eddie Heather, of the "B" team, and Bert Clayton, fifth and non-scoring "A" team man, rendered yeoman service.

Our Track Walk Captain, Percy Wright (recently proud father of a son and heir), still mans the A.A. guns, whilst Vice-Captain Eddie Heather is, we regret to write, in a sanatorium, but making progress.
Eddie Heather. Still making good progress and occasionally looks in at the Hall.
Eddie Heather, so the rumour goes, is now a father, who knows? Alan Bridger hopes to be walking on the road again after the war, with special attention to the "Brighton" and other distance events.
